task.title: Install the Node Maintenance Operator by using the CLI
task.shortdesc: You can use the OpenShift CLI (oc) to install the Node Maintenance Operator.

ul.li: Log in as a user with cluster-admin privileges.

context.p: You can install the Node Maintenance Operator in your own namespace or in the openshift-workload-availability namespace.

step.cmd: Create a Namespace CR for the Node Maintenance Operator:

substep.cmd: Define the Namespace CR and save the YAML file, for example, workload-availability-namespace.yaml:

info.codeblock: apiVersion: v1 kind: Namespace metadata: name: openshift-workload-availability

substep.cmd: To create the Namespace CR, run the following command:
Define the OperatorGroup CR and save the YAML file, for example, workload-availability-operator-group.yaml:

info.codeblock: apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1 kind: OperatorGroup metadata: name: workload-availability-operator-group namespace: openshift-workload-availability

substep.cmd: To create the OperatorGroup CR, run the following command:
Define the Subscription CR and save the YAML file, for example, node-maintenance-subscription.yaml:

info.codeblock: apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1alpha1 kind: Subscription metadata: name: node-maintenance-operator namespace: openshift-workload-availability spec: channel: stable installPlanApproval: Automatic name: node-maintenance-operator source: redhat-operators sourceNamespace: openshift-marketplace

ul.li:
namespace: Specify the Namespace where you want to install the Node Maintenance Operator.
To install the Node Maintenance Operator in the openshift-workload-availability namespace, specify openshift-workload-availability in the Subscription CR.

substep.cmd: To create the Subscription CR, run the following command:

ol.li: Verify that the installation succeeded by inspecting the CSV resource: $ oc get csv -n openshift-workload-availabilityNAME DISPLAY VERSION REPLACES PHASE node-maintenance-operator.v5.3.0 Node Maintenance Operator 5.3.0 node-maintenance-operator.v5.2.1 Succeeded

Verify that the Node Maintenance Operator is running: $ oc get deployment -n openshift-workload-availabilityNAME READY UP-TO-DATE AVAILABLE AGE node-maintenance-operator-controller-manager 1/1 1 1 10d
The Node Maintenance Operator is supported in a restricted network environment.
